results.claim: Running the sandbox inside an unprivileged container requires the nested-sandbox setting (`enableWeakerNestedSandbox`).

The cited code is accurate, as far as it goes.** `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180` — `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` holds exactly seven entries (`excludedCommands`, `deniedReadRoots`, `deniedWriteRoots`, `additionalWritableRoots`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `network`, `filesystem`); `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` is absent (verified `grep -ran`, zero hits anywhere in `packages/`). results.claim: The sandbox settings-file write denies resolve symlinks, so a symlink appearing at a protected settings path has its target added to the deny list for the next command.
results.quote: The deny rules resolve symlinks: when a symlink appears at a protected settings file path after startup, the sandbox adds its target to the deny list for the next command, so a linked settings file can't be edited through the link.
results.ourState: `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` builds the deny set lexically; the file contains no `realpath`, `lstat` or symlink handling, so a settings file symlinked out of the protected directory stays writable from inside the sandbox.

verdict.why:
REFUTED — textbook "the identifier really is unwired, but the consequence is false because something upstream already handled it".

1. DOC SENTENCE: verbatim, confirmed. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 478 contains the quoted sentence exactly. Reading the WHOLE line matters: it is gated `{/* min-version: 2.1.210 */}` and ends "Before v2.1.210, the deny rules didn't resolve symlinks." So this is a recent Claude addition — and we already match it.

2. CITED FILE: the literal claim about the file is TRUE but irrelevant. `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation/self-config-deny.ts:47` `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` does build its list with a plain `join`, and `grep -a` confirms the file has no `realpath`/`lstat`/`readlink`/`symlink`. It is a pure, platform-parameterised NAME LIST — canonicalisation is deliberately not its job.

3. ONE LAYER UP — the behaviour is implemented, in the single funnel every backend passes through. In `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts`:
- `:313-338` `resolveProcessIsolation` composes the write-deny set and terminates it with `.flatMap(root => denyRootPair(root, 'write'))` — so EVERY root `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` returns is piped through it, alongside the credential floor, the shared-git roots and the settings-file `deniedWriteRoots`.
- `:211-219` `denyRootPair` returns `[lexical, canonical]`, where `canonical = nearestExistingRealpath(resolve(root))`.
- `:113-130` `nearestExistingRealpath` is `realpathSync` with an ENOENT walk-up to the nearest existing ancestor (needed precisely because `<workspace>/.claude` and `/etc/nessy` usually do not exist), and an EACCES/EPERM fallback to the path as written.
- `:132-152` quotes the claimed sentence VERBATIM in the code comment as the reason both halves exist. We in fact go BEYOND the doc: Claude adds only the target; we keep the path AS WRITTEN too, because `unlink` acts on the link and not its target, so the link cannot be removed and replaced with an ordinary file at the protected name.

4. "for the next command" = per-spawn re-resolution, satisfied. `resolveProcessIsolation` is invoked inside `ProcessSupervisor.start` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:185`), so a link created after startup is re-paired before the next command is spawned.

5. POSITIVE CONTROL, run live on this darwin host — not a profile-text assertion but a real kernel test. `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.test.ts:327` ("refuses the protected path, refuses it through a symlink, and leaves a sibling alone") spawns real `/bin/bash` under the composed Seatbelt profile, symlinks `<workspace>/.claude -> <workspace>/linked-claude`, and asserts the write through the link fails with `Operation not permitted`, that `linked-claude/settings.json` was never created, that BOTH `(deny file-write* (subpath …))` entries appear in the profile, and that `rm` of the link itself is refused. A sibling `settings.json` in the same writable root still writes, so this is a deny of one tree and not a retreat to a read-only workspace. Result: `1 pass, 0 fail, 10 expect() calls`. `process-supervisor.test.ts:383,413` assert the same pair contract for the read and write deny paths.

The exact bypass the finding predicts ("a settings file symlinked out of the protected directory stays writable from inside the sandbox") is the scenario this test executes and measures as BLOCKED. Not an inert-worklist §3 owner decision and not a fork product difference — it is simply implemented, one call frame above the cited line.

Minor real nit, not a gap: the JSDoc block at `isolation.ts:132-152` documents `denyRootPair` but physically sits above `readAllowRootPair` (which has its own block at `:154-163`), leaving the actual `denyRootPair` at `:211` uncommented. Cosmetic doc drift only; behaviour is as tested.
verdict.correctedState: We DO resolve symlinks for the settings-file write denies, and we do it per spawn. `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation/self-config-deny.ts:47`) is intentionally a pure name list; canonicalisation is centralised one layer up in `resolveProcessIsolation` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts:313-338`), which pipes every deny root — self-config, credential floor, shared-git, settings-file `deniedWriteRoots` — through `denyRootPair` (`isolation.ts:211-219`). That returns the pair `[path-as-written, nearestExistingRealpath(path)]` (`isolation.ts:113-130`, `realpathSync` with an ENOENT walk-up for not-yet-created roots and an EACCES/EPERM fallback). `resolveProcessIsolation` runs inside `ProcessSupervisor.start` (`process-supervisor.ts:185`), i.e. once per command, which is the doc's "for the next command". We exceed the documented behaviour by also denying the link's own name so it cannot be unlinked and replaced. Proven end-to-end by a real sandboxed-`bash` darwin test at `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.test.ts:327`, which passes on this host.
